original_poem:
ਲੂਣਾ

ਜਿਸ ਦਿਨ ਸੂਰਜ ਨਵਾਂ ਚੜ੍ਹਿਆ,
ਅਸੀਂ ਬਾਬੇ ਨਾਲੋਂ ਸੁਣਿਆ ਸੀ,
ਇਹ ਧਰਤੀ ਕੁੜੀ ਜੰਮੀ ਹੈ,
ਪੈਰੀਆਂ ਨੀਂਹਾਂ ਰੱਖਦੀ ਹੈ।

ਜਦੋਂ ਵੇਲੇ ਦਿਨ ਢਲਿਆ ਸੀ,
ਤੇ ਬਾਬਾ ਪਿੰਡੋਂ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਸੀ,
ਆਪਣੀ ਕੁੜੀ ਦੇ ਜਨਮ ਦਾ ਸੋਗ,
ਮਾਂ ਵਾਂਗ ਬੜਾ ਕੁਝ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਸੀ,
ਲੂਣਾ ਸੀ ਧਰਤੀ ਦਾ ਨਾਮ,
ਤੇ ਸਾਡੇ ਪਿੰਡ ਦੀ ਢੱਲ ਹੀ ਸੀ।
translated_poem:
The day the new sun arose,
We heard from the village elder,
This earth has given birth to a daughter,
Who walks the path with humble steps.

When the day waned,
And the elder took his leave from the village,
He grieved the birth of his daughter,
As a mother would give so much,
Loona was the name of the earth,
And she was the slope of our village.

stanzas.loss_note: Stanza 1 in source is only the title word ਲੂਣਾ (Loona); the translation expands it into four lines that belong to stanza 2 in the source, creating a structural mismatch.

stanzas.loss_note: ਧਰਤੀ (dharti) carries the specific Punjabi weight of mother-earth as living, nurturing presence — not merely 'earth'; ਪੈਰੀਆਂ ਨੀਂਹਾਂ ਰੱਖਦੀ ਹੈ (walking with humble, foundational steps) is rendered as 'humble steps' losing the architectural metaphor of laying foundations.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: a daughter whose very steps lay the foundations of the village's future

stanzas.loss_note: No translation is available for stanza 3; key terms ਮਾਂ ਵਾਂਗ (like a mother), ਲੂਣਾ ਸੀ ਧਰਤੀ ਦਾ ਨਾਮ (Loona was the name of the earth), and ਢੱਲ (slope/decline) are unrendered — ਢੱਲ in Punjabi carries the double meaning of a hillside slope and the waning/decline of life.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: the daughter named as the earth itself, her identity inseparable from the land

cultural_entities.translation_note: Rendered as 'earth' — loses the Punjabi cultural weight of dharti as sacred mother-earth, a living feminine presence tied to village identity.
Rendered as 'village elder' — baaba in Punjabi village context carries specific patriarchal-ancestral authority beyond a generic elder.
No translation available; maan (mother) in Punjabi carries a culturally specific weight of selfless sacrifice tied to both biological and earth-mother symbolism.
